subject.title: AbeBooks withdrawal recovery misses live listings when mk row is absent

question: Should AbeBooks orphan withdrawal recovery rehydrate safe `mk_abebooks` rows for the existing withdraw cron, or send a direct AbeBooks close/quantity-zero job from the live snapshot?
rationale: Both routes can fix the live-listing gap, but they mutate production marketplace state for more than 10 listings and the repo policy requires a dry-run, samples, and human confirmation before that operational choice.

options.title: Rehydrate safe mk rows first
options.body: Build a dry-run reverse recovery that seeds only proven live, withdrawn book rows as `mk_abebooks` entries and lets the existing withdraw cron remove them.

options.title: Direct external close job
options.body: Use the snapshot/API evidence to send a dedicated AbeBooks close or quantity-zero operation without creating local mk rows first.

options.title: Manual seed only
options.body: Handle the current cohort manually and defer a reusable recovery path, reducing code scope but leaving the systemic gap open.

recommendation.title: Rehydrate safe mk rows first
recommendation.body: Build a dry-run reverse recovery that seeds only proven live, withdrawn book rows as `mk_abebooks` entries and lets the existing withdraw cron remove them.

likelyOwner.reason: Javier has the strongest AbeBooks-specific withdraw history and recent raw withdraw logging context for choosing the operational recovery route.
